newsitem.title: UK: FEATURE - Britain's royal family goes multimedia.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - Britain's royal family goes multimedia.

text.p: It's a saga that has thrilled and titillated millions for much of the past century with its romances, weddings, tragedies and divorces.
From the reign of Queen Victoria through the abdication of Edward VIII and the doomed marriage of Prince Charles and Princess Diana, Britain's royal family has been front-page news.
Now it's all available on CD-ROM.

"Fourteen Weddings and a Divorce", a play on the title of the successful British film "Four Weddings and a Funeral", charts the history of the royal family in the 20th century with more than an hour of video clips, archive recordings, print cuttings, dozens of pictures and 10,000 words of text.
"The combination of multimedia and royals is a good one," said Adrian Munsey, managing director of Odyssey Video which produced the CD-ROM.
"It initially was "14 Weddings and a Funeral', but then we thought we should change it to "divorce' because they were coming through thick and fast."
To the accompaniment of Edward Elgar's "Land of Hope and Glory" and the British national anthem, the CD-ROM opens with a montage of events in the lives of members of the House of Windsor.

Divided into five catagories -- major world events, royal biographies, weddings and a divorce, major royal events and the royal atlas, the CD-ROM is billed as one of the most comprehensive products ever made about the royal family.
Odyssey, which had already produced seven television documentaries on the royals, formed a team of five journalists to work on it.
"We really pursued all the printed and unprinted sources. There's quite a lot of good gossip in it," said Munsey.
Designed to appeal to history buffs as well as royal watchers, little known, steamy details of the love lives of some long-gone royals add considerable spice to the product.
The antics of modern day royals pale in comparison to what some of their ancestors were up to.
Queen Victoria's consort, Prince Albert, regarded in his day as a paragon of virtue, had a metal ring pierced through his penis, according to the CD-ROM.

"Whether this was to increase Queen Victoria's and his own satisfaction or, in conjunction with a piece of thread tied around his thigh, to govern unscheduled erections...can best be answered by contemporary wearers of this unconventional adornment," Odyssey said in a statement.

Victoria's son Edward VII had countless mistresses before he became king and liked them to be carried into his banquet hall on a silver platter, naked except for a few carefully placed sprigs of parsley.

George V, Victoria's grandson, shared a mistress with his older brother Prince Albert Victor, known to his family as Eddy, whose homosexual exploits with his Cambridge University tutor were lampooned in Punch magazine.
The Duchess of Windsor's first husband, U.S. aviator Win Spencer, reportedly took his then wife to brothels in Hong Kong so she could learn the prostitutes' sexual techniques.
"According to some sources it was the duchess's way with the hot oils of Fang Chung that caused Edward VIII to abdicate," Odyssey said.
With profiles of 28 royals ranging from Queen Victoria to Princess Diana's youngest son Prince Henry, "Fourteen Weddings and a Divorce" is an exhaustive depository of royal information.
Prince Charles's screen profile includes his schooldays, investiture as the Prince of Wales, his years as an "action man", and his lovers and girlfriends.
Diana's profile features fashion, her children, charity work as well as little known details on her former boyfriends and male admirers.
Romances of all the members of the royal family loom large.
The CD-ROM delves into the agony of Princess Margaret, Queen Elizabeth's younger sister, who ended her relationship with a divorced military captain because of public and royal pressure.

Queen Elizabeth is shown as a 20-year-old princess frustrated by the father's refusal to allow her to marry Prince Philip. It was only due the intervention of her grandmother Queen Mary that he relented.
"Fourteen Weddings and a Divorce" has already been released in Britain and overseas distribution deals are being negotiated for the United States, Japan and Germany.
"We've tried to make it a CD-ROM and a book and a video as well, so you can watch it on a variety of levels," said Munsey. "You can't overestimate how much interest there is in this subject."
